## What is Svelte?

Svelte is a new way to build web applications. It's a compiler that takes your declarative components and converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM.

Learn more at the [Svelte website](https://svelte.dev), or stop by the [Discord chatroom](https://svelte.dev/chat).

## Supporting Svelte

Svelte is an MIT-licensed open source project with its ongoing development made possible entirely by fantastic volunteers. If you'd like to support their efforts, please consider:

- [Becoming a backer on Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/svelte).

Funds donated via Open Collective will be used for compensating expenses related to Svelte's development such as hosting costs. If sufficient donations are received, funds may also be used to support Svelte's development more directly.

## Roadmap

You may view [our roadmap](https://svelte.dev/roadmap) if you'd like to see what we're currently working on.

## Contributing

Please see the [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [`svelte`](packages/svelte) package for information on contributing to Svelte.

## Is svelte.dev down?

Probably not, but it's possible. If you can't seem to access any `.dev` sites, check out [this SuperUser question and answer](https://superuser.com/q/1413402).

# [jQuery](https://jquery.com/) — New Wave JavaScript

Meetings are currently held on the [matrix.org platform](https://matrix.to/#/#jquery_meeting:gitter.im).

Meeting minutes can be found at [meetings.jquery.org](https://meetings.jquery.org/category/core/).

The latest version of jQuery is available at [https://jquery.com/download/](https://jquery.com/download/).

## Version support

| Version | Branch     | Support       |
| ------- | ---------- | ------------- |
| 4.x     | main       | Full          |
| 3.x     | 3.x-stable | Critical-only |
| 2.x     | 2.x-stable | None          |
| 1.x     | 1.x-stable | None          |

[jQuery 4.0.0 has been released!](https://blog.jquery.com/2026/01/17/jquery-4-0-0/)

The 3.x branch will now only receive critical updates. The 2.x and 1.x branches are no longer supported. We recommend that all users upgrade to the latest version of jQuery to ensure that they have the best performance, security, and features.

Commercial support for previous versions is available from [HeroDevs](https://www.herodevs.com/support/jquery-nes?utm_source=jQuery&utm_medium=link&utm_campaign=eol_support_jQuery) or [TuxCare](https://tuxcare.com/lp/click-jquery-support/).

Learn more about our [version support](https://jquery.com/support/).

## Contribution Guides

In the spirit of open source software development, jQuery always encourages community code contribution. To help you get started and before you jump into writing code, be sure to read these important contribution guidelines thoroughly:

1. [Getting Involved](https://contribute.jquery.org/)
2. [Core Style Guide](https://contribute.jquery.org/style-guide/js/)
3. [Writing Code for jQuery Projects](https://contribute.jquery.org/code/)

### References to issues/PRs

GitHub issues/PRs are usually referenced via `gh-NUMBER`, where `NUMBER` is the numerical ID of the issue/PR. You can find such an issue/PR under `https://github.com/jquery/jquery/issues/NUMBER`.

jQuery has used a different bug tracker - based on Trac - in the past, available under [bugs.jquery.com](https://bugs.jquery.com/). It is being kept in read only mode so that referring to past discussions is possible. When jQuery source references one of those issues, it uses the pattern `trac-NUMBER`, where `NUMBER` is the numerical ID of the issue. You can find such an issue under `https://bugs.jquery.com/ticket/NUMBER`.

## Environments in which to use jQuery

- [Browser support](https://jquery.com/browser-support/)
- jQuery also supports Node, browser extensions, and other non-browser environments.

## What you need to build your own jQuery

To build jQuery, you need to have the latest Node.js/npm and git 1.7 or later. Earlier versions might work, but are not supported.

For Windows, you have to download and install [git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) and [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/).

macOS users should install [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/). Once Homebrew is installed, run `brew install git` to install git,
and `brew install node` to install Node.js.

Linux/BSD users should use their appropriate package managers to install git and Node.js, or build from source
if you swing that way. Easy-peasy.

## How to build your own jQuery

First, [clone the jQuery git repo](https://help.github.com/en/github/creating-cloning-and-archiving-repositories/cloning-a-repository).

Then, enter the jquery directory, install dependencies, and run the build script:

```bash
cd jquery
npm install
npm run build
```

The built version of jQuery will be placed in the `dist/` directory, along with a minified copy and associated map file.

## Build all jQuery release files

To build all variants of jQuery, run the following command:

```bash
npm run build:all
```

This will create all of the variants that jQuery includes in a release, including `jquery.js`, `jquery.slim.js`, `jquery.module.js`, and `jquery.slim.module.js` along their associated minified files and sourcemaps.

`jquery.module.js` and `jquery.slim.module.js` are [ECMAScript modules](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules) that export `jQuery` and `$` as named exports are placed in the `dist-module/` directory rather than the `dist/` directory.

## Building a Custom jQuery

The build script can be used to create a custom version of jQuery that includes only the modules you need.

Any module may be excluded except for `core`. When excluding `selector`, it is not removed but replaced with a small wrapper around native `querySelectorAll` (see below for more information).

### Build Script Help

To see the full list of available options for the build script, run the following:

```bash
npm run build -- --help
```

### Modules

To exclude a module, pass its path relative to the `src` folder (without the `.js` extension) to the `--exclude` option. When using the `--include` option, the default includes are dropped and a build is created with only those modules.

Some example modules that can be excluded or included are:

- **ajax**: All AJAX functionality: `$.ajax()`, `$.get()`, `$.post()`, `$.ajaxSetup()`, `.load()`, transports, and ajax event shorthands such as `.ajaxStart()`.
- **ajax/xhr**: The XMLHttpRequest AJAX transport only.
- **ajax/script**: The `<script>` AJAX transport only; used to retrieve scripts.
- **ajax/jsonp**: The JSONP AJAX transport only; depends on the ajax/script transport.
- **css**: The `.css()` method. Also removes **all** modules depending on css (including **effects**, **dimensions**, and **offset**).
- **css/showHide**: Non-animated `.show()`, `.hide()` and `.toggle()`; can be excluded if you use classes or explicit `.css()` calls to set the `display` property. Also removes the **effects** module.
- **deprecated**: Methods documented as deprecated but not yet removed.
- **dimensions**: The `.width()` and `.height()` methods, including `inner-` and `outer-` variations.
- **effects**: The `.animate()` method and its shorthands such as `.slideUp()` or `.hide("slow")`.
- **event**: The `.on()` and `.off()` methods and all event functionality.
- **event/trigger**: The `.trigger()` and `.triggerHandler()` methods.
- **offset**: The `.offset()`, `.position()`, `.offsetParent()`, `.scrollLeft()`, and `.scrollTop()` methods.
- **wrap**: The `.wrap()`, `.wrapAll()`, `.wrapInner()`, and `.unwrap()` methods.
- **core/ready**: Exclude the ready module if you place your scripts at the end of the body. Any ready callbacks bound with `jQuery()` will simply be called immediately. However, `jQuery(document).ready()` will not be a function and `.on("ready", ...)` or similar will not be triggered.
- **deferred**: Exclude jQuery.Deferred. This also excludes all modules that rely on Deferred, including **ajax**, **effects**, and **queue**, but replaces **core/ready** with **core/ready-no-deferred**.
- **exports/global**: Exclude the attachment of global jQuery variables ($ and jQuery) to the window.
- **exports/amd**: Exclude the AMD definition.

- **selector**: The full jQuery selector engine. When this module is excluded, it is replaced with a rudimentary selector engine based on the browser's `querySelectorAll` method that does not support jQuery selector extensions or enhanced semantics. See the [selector-native.js](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/main/src/selector-native.js) file for details.

*Note*: Excluding the full `selector` module will also exclude all jQuery selector extensions (such as `effects/animatedSelector` and `css/hiddenVisibleSelectors`).

##### AMD name

You can set the module name for jQuery's AMD definition. By default, it is set to "jquery", which plays nicely with plugins and third-party libraries, but there may be cases where you'd like to change this. Pass it to the `--amd` parameter:

```bash
npm run build -- --amd="custom-name"
```

Or, to define anonymously, leave the name blank.

```bash
npm run build -- --amd
```

##### File name and directory

The default name for the built jQuery file is `jquery.js`; it is placed under the `dist/` directory. It's possible to change the file name using `--filename` and the directory using `--dir`. `--dir` is relative to the project root.

```bash
npm run build -- --slim --filename="jquery.slim.js" --dir="/tmp"
```

This would create a slim version of jQuery and place it under `tmp/jquery.slim.js`.

##### ECMAScript Module (ESM) mode

By default, jQuery generates a regular script JavaScript file. You can also generate an ECMAScript module exporting `jQuery` as the default export using the `--esm` parameter:

```bash
npm run build -- --filename=jquery.module.js --esm
```

##### Factory mode

By default, jQuery depends on a global `window`. For environments that don't have one, you can generate a factory build that exposes a function accepting `window` as a parameter that you can provide externally (see [`README` of the published package](build/fixtures/README.md) for usage instructions). You can generate such a factory using the `--factory` parameter:

```bash
npm run build -- --filename=jquery.factory.js --factory
```

This option can be mixed with others like `--esm` or `--slim`:

```bash
npm run build -- --filename=jquery.factory.slim.module.js --factory --esm --slim --dir="/dist-module"
```

#### Custom Build Examples

Create a custom build using `npm run build`, listing the modules to be excluded. Excluding a top-level module also excludes its corresponding directory of modules.

Exclude all **ajax** functionality:

```bash
npm run build -- --exclude=ajax
```

Excluding **css** removes modules depending on CSS: **effects**, **offset**, **dimensions**.

```bash
npm run build -- --exclude=css
```

Exclude a bunch of modules (`-e` is an alias for `--exclude`):

```bash
npm run build -- -e ajax/jsonp -e css -e deprecated -e dimensions -e effects -e offset -e wrap
```

There is a special alias to generate a build with the same configuration as the official jQuery Slim build:

```bash
npm run build -- --filename=jquery.slim.js --slim
```

Or, to create the slim build as an esm module:

```bash
npm run build -- --filename=jquery.slim.module.js --slim --esm
```

*Non-official custom builds are not regularly tested. Use them at your own risk.*

## Running the Unit Tests

Make sure you have the necessary dependencies:

```bash
npm install
```

Start `npm start` to auto-build jQuery as you work:

```bash
npm start
```

Run the unit tests with a local server that supports PHP. Ensure that you run the site from the root directory, not the "test" directory. No database is required. Pre-configured php local servers are available for Windows and Mac. Here are some options:

- Windows: [WAMP download](https://www.wampserver.com/en/)
- Mac: [MAMP download](https://www.mamp.info/en/downloads/)
- Linux: [Setting up LAMP](https://www.linux.com/training-tutorials/easy-lamp-server-installation/)
- [Mongoose (most platforms)](https://code.google.com/p/mongoose/)

## Essential Git

As the source code is handled by the Git version control system, it's useful to know some features used.

### Cleaning

If you want to purge your working directory back to the status of upstream, the following commands can be used (remember everything you've worked on is gone after these):

```bash
git reset --hard upstream/main
git clean -fdx
```

### Rebasing

For feature/topic branches, you should always use the `--rebase` flag to `git pull`, or if you are usually handling many temporary "to be in a github pull request" branches, run the following to automate this:

```bash
git config branch.autosetuprebase local
```

(see `man git-config` for more information)

### Handling merge conflicts

If you're getting merge conflicts when merging, instead of editing the conflicted files manually, you can use the feature
`git mergetool`. Even though the default tool `xxdiff` looks awful/old, it's rather useful.

The following are some commands that can be used there:

- `Ctrl + Alt + M` - automerge as much as possible
- `b` - jump to next merge conflict
- `s` - change the order of the conflicted lines
- `u` - undo a merge
- `left mouse button` - mark a block to be the winner
- `middle mouse button` - mark a line to be the winner
- `Ctrl + S` - save
- `Ctrl + Q` - quit

## [QUnit](https://api.qunitjs.com) Reference

### Test methods

```js
expect( numAssertions );
stop();
start();
```

*Note*: QUnit's eventual addition of an argument to stop/start is ignored in this test suite so that start and stop can be passed as callbacks without worrying about their parameters.

### Test assertions

```js
ok( value, [message] );
equal( actual, expected, [message] );
notEqual( actual, expected, [message] );
deepEqual( actual, expected, [message] );
notDeepEqual( actual, expected, [message] );
strictEqual( actual, expected, [message] );
notStrictEqual( actual, expected, [message] );
throws( block, [expected], [message] );
```

## Test Suite Convenience Methods Reference

See [test/data/testinit.js](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/main/test/data/testinit.js).

### Returns an array of elements with the given IDs

```js
q( ... );
```

Example:

```js
q( "main", "foo", "bar" );

=> [ div#main, span#foo, input#bar ]
```

### Asserts that a selection matches the given IDs

```js
t( testName, selector, [ "array", "of", "ids" ] );
```

Example:

```js
t("Check for something", "//[a]", ["foo", "bar"]);
```

### Fires a native DOM event without going through jQuery

```js
fireNative( node, eventType );
```

Example:

```js
fireNative( jQuery( "#elem" )[ 0 ], "click" );
```

### Add random number to url to stop caching

```js
url( "some/url" );
```

Example:

```js
url( "index.html" );

=> "data/index.html?10538358428943"


url( "mock.php?foo=bar" );

=> "data/mock.php?foo=bar&10538358345554"
```

### Run tests in an iframe

Some tests may require a document other than the standard test fixture, and
these can be run in a separate iframe. The actual test code and assertions
remain in jQuery's main test files; only the minimal test fixture markup
and setup code should be placed in the iframe file.

```js
testIframe( testName, fileName,
  function testCallback(
      assert, jQuery, window, document,
	  [ additional args ] ) {
	...
  } );
```

This loads a page, constructing a url with fileName `"./data/" + fileName`.
The iframed page determines when the callback occurs in the test by
including the "/test/data/iframeTest.js" script and calling
`startIframeTest( [ additional args ] )` when appropriate. Often this
will be after either document ready or `window.onload` fires.

The `testCallback` receives the QUnit `assert` object created by `testIframe`
for this test, followed by the global `jQuery`, `window`, and `document` from
the iframe. If the iframe code passes any arguments to `startIframeTest`,
they follow the `document` argument.

## Questions?

If you have any questions, please feel free to ask on the
[Developing jQuery Core forum](https://forum.jquery.com/developing-jquery-core) or in #jquery on [libera](https://web.libera.chat/).

## Install ECC

> [!IMPORTANT]
> ECC 2.2 includes guided package setup for Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code.
> The universal package requires Node.js 18 or newer. Claude plugin setup also
> requires Git and Claude Code 2.1 or newer on `PATH`.

### Recommended: universal guided setup

For Claude Code plugin setup, updates, scope changes, and hook-profile changes:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup
```

#### Windows first-time walkthrough

If you are new to command-line tools, use this copy-and-paste path:

1. Install Node.js 18 or newer, Git, and Claude Code.
2. Open **PowerShell** from the Windows Start menu.
3. Confirm that each prerequisite is available:

   ```powershell
   node --version
   git --version
   claude --version
   ```

4. Run the guided installer:

   ```powershell
   npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup
   ```

5. For a typical personal setup, choose **Global user**, choose **Standard** hooks, and confirm.
6. Start a new Claude Code session and run `/plugin list` to verify that `ecc@ecc` is enabled.

This path does not require cloning the repository. If any prerequisite command is not found, install or repair that prerequisite before rerunning ECC setup.

If npm reports a version or cache error, confirm the registry version before retrying:

```bash
npm view ecc-universal version
```

ECC 2.2 supports the same guided setup through modern package runners:

| Package runner | Guided setup command |
|---|---|
| npm / npx | `npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| pnpm | `pnpm dlx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| Yarn 2+ | `yarn dlx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |
| Bun | `bunx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` |

The examples select [the published ECC 2.2.3 release](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ecc-universal/v/2.2.3), matching this repository's release version. A version pin is not a security audit or an integrity check. Review the release source and registry integrity before running package code; use a reviewed checkout for unreleased changes.

Yarn Classic 1 does not provide `yarn dlx`; use `npx`, install the package globally, or upgrade Yarn for a temporary one-shot run.

The wizard inventories the official marketplace and every native Claude install scope before making changes, then installs, updates, or safely moves `ecc@ecc` to the scope you choose. Rerun the same command whenever you want to update ECC, change scope, or change its hook profile. This setup wizard currently configures the Claude Code plugin; use the multi-harness wizard below for Codex or Kimi Code.

To configure more than one coding agent in one reviewed flow, use the multi-harness wizard:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided
```

It lets you select any combination of Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code, shows each install channel and destination, preflights every selection before the first write, and asks for one final confirmation.

| Harness | Guided install behavior |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Native `ecc@ecc` plugin with one `user`, `project`, or `local` scope and an ECC hook profile |
| Codex | Native Codex marketplace/plugin lifecycle; hook review and trust remain Codex-owned |
| Kimi Code | Managed project files under `./.kimi-code`; ECC hooks, model/provider settings, and authentication are not configured |

For automation, make every provider-specific choice explicit:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided \
  --harness claude --harness codex --harness kimi \
  --claude-scope local --claude-hooks standard \
  --profile core --yes
```

Verify the native guided Codex path and managed Kimi path without writing first:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --guided --harness codex --dry-run
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --profile core --target kimi --dry-run
```

Additional package-name commands are also available through the 2.2 alias:

```bash
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 consult "security reviews" --target claude
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 install --profile minimal --target claude --with capability:machine-learning
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 doctor --target kimi
```

Do not use `npx ecc-install --profile minimal --target claude`: `ecc-install` is a binary name inside `ecc-universal`, not a separately published npm package.

ECC also ships advanced managed adapters for `cursor`, `antigravity`, `antigravity-home`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `codebuddy`, `joycode`, `qwen`, `zed`, `hermes`, `openclaw`, and `mistral-vibe`. Those targets still use their documented `ecc install --target ...` paths until each adapter has passed the guided collision, update, repair, and uninstall lifecycle matrix. Neither wizard silently installs into every detected harness.

### Pick one path only (per harness)

You can use ECC with Claude Code, Codex, and other harnesses at the same time. Choose one install method for each harness:

- **Recommended default:** run the guided Claude plugin setup above
- **Also supported for Claude Code:** use the [native plugin commands](#claude-code-details)
- **Available in release 2.2:** guided package setup for Claude Code, Codex, and Kimi Code
- **Works:** Claude Code plugin + Codex native plugin
- **Works:** Claude Code plugin + the legacy Codex sync flow
- **Avoid:** Claude Code plugin + full Claude manual install
- **Avoid:** Codex sync + Codex marketplace plugin

**Do not stack install methods.** Installing ECC twice into the same harness can duplicate skills, commands, hooks, or configuration; installing it once into multiple harnesses does not.

If you already layered multiple installs and things look duplicated, skip straight to [Reset / Uninstall ECC](#reset--uninstall-ecc).

**Install trouble?** Open the short [install or runtime problem form](https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC/issues/new?template=install-problem.yml), or run `ecc feedback`. ECC never uploads diagnostics automatically.

### Claude Code details

Alternatively, run Claude Code's native plugin commands inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC
/plugin install ecc@ecc
```

The native path installs ECC's skills, agents, commands, and plugin-managed hooks. If you choose it, stop there. Do not also run a full manual install into Claude Code.

Claude Code owns these built-in commands, including their errors when a marketplace, plugin, or conflicting scope already exists. ECC cannot intercept that parser. If either native command reports an existing install or scope conflict, use the 2.2 guided setup or resolve the conflicting Claude plugin scope before retrying; do not layer a manual install on top.

After ECC is installed, `/ecc:configure-ecc` is the namespaced in-Claude reconfiguration skill. It delegates to the same safe setup flow, but it is available only after the plugin is installed and cannot replace Claude Code's built-in `/plugin` command during a first install.

Claude Code plugins cannot distribute `rules`, so add only the rule packs you actually want:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC.git
cd ECC
mkdir -p ~/.claude/rules/ecc
cp -R rules/common ~/.claude/rules/ecc/
cp -R rules/typescript ~/.claude/rules/ecc/  # replace with your stack
```

Start with `rules/common` plus one language or framework pack you actually use. If you install the plugin, do not run `./install.sh --profile full` afterward.

<details>
<summary><strong>Prefer settings.json? Add the marketplace declaratively</strong></summary>

Add directly to your `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
    "ecc": {
      "source": {
        "source": "github",
        "repo": "affaan-m/ECC"
      }
    }
  },
  "enabledPlugins": {
    "ecc@ecc": true
  }
}
```

This gives you the same result as the two `/plugin` commands above.
</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Naming + migration note (ecc@ecc, affaan-m/ECC, ecc-universal)</strong></summary>

ECC has three public identifiers, and they are not interchangeable:

- GitHub source repo: `affaan-m/ECC`
- Claude marketplace/plugin identifier: `ecc@ecc`
- npm package: `ecc-universal`

This is intentional. Anthropic marketplace/plugin installs are keyed by a canonical plugin identifier, so ECC uses `ecc@ecc` to keep tool names and slash-command namespaces short enough for strict Desktop/API validators. Older posts may still show the former long marketplace identifier; treat that as a legacy alias only. Separately, the npm package stayed on `ecc-universal`, so npm installs and marketplace installs intentionally use different names.

npm releases are cut per version tag, not per commit, so `ecc-universal` tracks releases (2.1, 2.2, ...) rather than every push to `main`. Install from git if you want the bleeding edge.

If your local Claude setup was wiped or reset, that does not mean you need to repurchase anything. Start with `node scripts/ecc.js list-installed`, then run `node scripts/ecc.js doctor` and `node scripts/ecc.js repair` before reinstalling. That usually restores ECC-managed files without rebuilding your setup.
</details>

## Why It's Fun to Explore

Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry:
- *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"*
- *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"*
- *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"*

**Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time.

---

### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders

- **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory.
- **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Jiaozhi Province in Annam (1407 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible.
- **Reigning Monarch on the Timeline**: The bubble above the timeline names the monarch on the throne in the current year (e.g. `100 BCE · Western Han · Emp. Wu`, `630 CE · Tang · Emp. Taizong`, `1700 CE · Qing · Kangxi Emp. (Shengzu)`); the Chinese interface also shows the regnal era year (`唐太宗·贞观四年`).
- **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern Province Overlay**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents. In the top-right **Layers** menu, `Provinces` (on by default) draws today's provincial boundaries over the historical map, and `Prov. Names` adds their names.
- **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era; ancient coastlines around the Bohai Gulf, northern Jiangsu, the Yangtze estuary, and the Pearl River Delta also advance and retreat by era.
- **Zoomable Timeline**: Drag the handles at either end of the timeline inward to zoom into one stretch of history (handy for short eras such as Qin, the Three Kingdoms, or the Five Dynasties); double-click the timeline to return to the full overview.
- **Voice Narration**: Turn on the narration toggle next to the play button and autoplay reads out each year and its events in the browser's built-in voice; it also follows a person's chronicle on autoplay (requires a browser with speech synthesis).

![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp)

---

### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`)

**Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card:
- **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks.
- **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Chronicles`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year!
- **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*.

> [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en)

![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp)

---

### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space

Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, marking every milestone of their life with numbered pins across changing dynastic borders:
- **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map!
- **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi.
- **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains.
- **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an.
- **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu.
- **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island.
- **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an.
- **Multi-Person Chronicles**: Type two or three names into the search box (e.g. `Li Bai, Du Fu, Gao Shi` or `Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan`) to merge their journeys onto one timeline. Places where they met in the same year are marked as shared encounters, and the `Shared N` pill narrows the list to just those stops.
- **Event Storylines**: Major events unfold stop by stop, just like a person's life. The Chu–Han Contention (207–202 BCE), the An Lushan Rebellion (755–763 CE) and the Jingkang Catastrophe (1125–1142 CE) are each laid out in ten stops across three acts, with the two sides drawn in different colors so each side's advances are easy to follow.

Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site.

![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp)

---

### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn?

Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**):
- **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the **`Confirm ↵`** chip next to the pin to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates!
- Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**.

## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links

### Keyboard Shortcuts

| Key / Action | Effect |

## Why openGym

Most workout apps keep your data on their servers, push you towards a subscription, or vanish
when the company does. openGym runs on your own box, keeps your data in a folder you control, and
is yours to fork. It still behaves like a modern app: installable on the home screen, passkey
sign-in, works offline, syncs between your phone and your laptop.

No account on someone else's server, no subscription, no ads, no telemetry. One
`docker compose up` and it's running.

The [in-browser demo](https://opengym.ch/demo/) is the real app with example data,
if you want to try it before installing anything.

## Features

**Planning**

- A routine per weekday over a library of **over 5,600 exercises** with animated demos, searchable and
  browsable by muscle on a body map. Filter by the equipment you own.
- Four starter plans (Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, 5×5) that load as ordinary,
  editable routines.
- Every session on the Plan page and today's on Home carries a tiny body map with the muscles it
  works lit up, so you know Leg Day is legs before you open it.
- Move a session to another day without touching the weekly plan. The week starts on Monday or
  Sunday, your choice.
- Or skip the weekdays altogether: a **rotation** (A, B, C, A, ...) where the next session is
  simply the next one you haven't done, however the week went.
- Supersets, warm-up sets, drop sets and rest-pause, timed exercises (planks, hangs, carries),
  cardio by time and speed, rest time per exercise, planned deloads.
- Your own exercises, with your own photo, GIF or short video. Location data is stripped on the
  device before upload.

**Training**

- Guided sessions: today's workout starts itself, weights are pre-filled from last time, a rest
  timer runs between sets, PRs are detected as you go. On a rest day it tells you when the next
  session is.
- A quiet workout screen: one menu per exercise, the set number as the set's own menu, card or
  list view. Switches in Settings bring the old button rows back if you liked them.
- Optional effort column as RIR or RPE, colour-coded, with a plain-language line per level.
- Plate math for barbell, EZ bar, trap bar and Smith machine, worked out from the plates you own.
  Train in more than one place? Each gym keeps its own plates, dumbbells, bars and machine stacks,
  and the phone can switch to the gym you just walked into.
- Bodyweight exercises know they carry no load: log reps, add a dip belt if you use one.
- Per-side reps for lunges and single-arm work, the screen stays awake while you train, and a
  rest-timer alert can flash the screen for loud gyms.
- Swipe a set left to delete it (with Undo) or right to copy it. Pyramid sets with their own reps
  and rest per set, and a scroll wheel for any rest time up to 15 minutes, or no timer at all.
- Machine taken? A planned backup exercise swaps in with one tap and keeps the slot's sets and reps.
  Machines can carry their real weight stack, odd steps included, and progression sticks to it.
- The session's volume runs live at the end of the progress bar.

**Progress**

- Progression rules per routine or per exercise: linear, Greyskull LP, double progression through a
  visible rep range, triple progression (reps, then sets, then load), or adding time. Each target explains why it is that number; missed reps never
  add load, stalls trigger a deload.
- Estimated 1RM per exercise with its own curve, Structural Balance ratios (Poliquin, Thibaudeau,
  ATG), a year-long activity heatmap.
- A muscle map in three modes: where your volume went, what is still recovering, and what has gone
  untrained.
- Body-weight chart against a goal line, with your weekly rate and an optional lose, gain or hold
  range, and progress photos on a timeline with a before/after slider.
- Lifts as a percentage of body weight, and a running total of everything you've ever lifted.
- Edit any saved workout after the fact, log one you did on paper, or move it to the right date.
  Records are re-read from the corrected history.

**Accounts and data**

- Passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint) with per-profile data synced across devices. Password
  sign-in can be switched on per instance; new devices pair with a one-time code or QR.
- Two devices editing at once merge field by field instead of overwriting each other (see
  [sync](#how-sync-works)).
- Import from FitNotes, Strong, Hevy (CSV or API key) and Apple Health weight exports. Export
  everything as one JSON file, or your workouts and body data as a spreadsheet (CSV).
- Share a plan as a small file or print it as a PDF.
- Optional admin dashboard with invite-only signup and an activity log.
- 26 languages, including right-to-left Arabic and Persian, and Traditional Chinese. Exercise names and
  instructions are translated for most of them.

**On the phone and the wrist**

- Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android that work on their own (no server, no account) or connected to
  yours. Rest timer in the notification shade, reminders, and Health Connect or Apple Health in both
  directions: workouts go out, weigh-ins and heart rate per set come back in.
- A gym reminder, off by default: walk into one of your gyms and the phone nudges you to hit
  Start. Once a day at most, never after you trained, and your gyms stay on the phone.
- An Apple Watch app: tick off sets with the Digital Crown, RPE or RIR right on the wrist, a
  full-screen rest countdown, heart rate per set, a Lock button against stray crown presses, and
  complications. No watch? AirPods Pro 3 do the heart rate on iOS 26.
- Widgets and a Live Activity on the iPhone: log a set, skip the rest or jump to the next exercise
  from the Lock Screen without opening the app.

**Only what you use**

- [Modules](docs/MODULES.md): switch whole parts of the app on and off in Settings → Modules, from
  "Just training" to "Everything". Body, Health, Motivation, the Coach, seasonal themes and more
  each disappear completely while they're off, and nothing is deleted.

**Optional extras, off by default**

- An [AI coach](docs/AI_COACH.md) that drafts a week of routines and later suggests changes based on
  what you logged, and answers questions about your training. You approve every change. It runs
  on your server, or on the phone alone, with your own provider key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or
  any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama included).
- An [MCP server](mcp/README.md) so an assistant like Claude Desktop can answer questions about your
  training history, and log a workout you describe to it. Local; not part of the Docker build.
- [Integrations](docs/INTEGRATIONS.md) in one place: Apple Health, Health Connect (Garmin, Fitbit,
  Withings and friends come in through them), imports, and signed webhooks to Home Assistant, n8n or
  ntfy when you finish a workout, set a record or weigh in.

The full list of what changed release by release is in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

## Quick start

You need [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with Compose.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym
cd openGym
cp .env.example .env
docker compose pull      # prebuilt images, amd64 + arm64 (skip this to build from source)
docker compose up -d
```

Open <http://localhost:8080>, tap **Create profile**, and you're in. The exercise animations are
part of the image, so there's nothing else to download.

To reach it from your phone with passkeys you need HTTPS on a domain; that's a two-line change in
`.env`. The [self-hosting guide](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) walks through Cloudflare Tunnel, Caddy,
Traefik and nginx, and there are separate guides for
[HTTPS on a LAN](docs/SELF_HOSTING_HTTPS.md), [a Mac with Tailscale](docs/SELF_HOSTING_MAC.md) and [Kubernetes](docs/SELF_HOSTING_KUBERNETES.md).

> [!NOTE]
> Images are published from the same tag to `ghcr.io/duartesantos8/opengym-{api,web}`
> (what `docker-compose.yml` pulls) and `registry.gitlab.com/duartesantos8/opengym/{api,web}`. Swap
> the `image:` lines if you prefer GitLab's registry, or run `docker compose up -d --build` to build
> locally. Either way you don't need Node on the host.

| `NGINX_PORT` | Port the web container listens on inside the container | `80` |

| `PASSWORD_LOGIN` | Offer name-and-password sign-in next to passkeys | *(off)* |

`/data` inside the container and mapped to `./data` on the host; change the volume, not the
variable. The [self-hosting guide](docs/SELF_HOSTING.md) covers every option in detail.

</details>

## Phone app

The same codebase builds the phone apps with Capacitor. Use them on their own (everything stays on
the phone, no account) or connect them to your server and sync.

| | Get it |
|---|---|
| **iPhone and iPad**, with the **Apple Watch** app | The [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6822275400), in every App Store country |
| **Android** | The signed APK from the [latest release](https://github.com/DuarteSantos8/openGym/releases/latest) or [opengym.ch](https://opengym.ch), in three sizes: **Standard** (`openGym-X.Y.Z.apk`, animations at 180 px, about 315 MB), **Plus** (`openGym-Plus-X.Y.Z.apk`, 240 px, about 424 MB) and **HD** (`openGym-HD-X.Y.Z.apk`, 360 px, about 760 MB). It updates itself and stays the kind you picked |
| **Google Play** | In closed testing: Google wants 12 testers for 14 days before it lets everyone in. Join the [tester group](https://groups.google.com/g/opengym-testers/about), then [opt in](https://play.google.com/apps/testing/ch.duartesantos.opengym). It installs right over the APK and keeps your data |
| **Wear OS watch** (beta) | Rides along with the Google Play test: once Google's watch review is done, "openGym Beta" shows up in the Play Store on your Galaxy Watch, Pixel Watch and friends. Details: [docs/WEAR_OS.md](docs/WEAR_OS.md) |

Every APK sits next to its `.sha256`. The APK and the Play app share one signing key, so you can
switch between them (or between Standard, Plus and HD) without losing data. Details, building it
yourself and connecting to your server: [docs/MOBILE.md](docs/MOBILE.md).

## How it works

<p align="center">
<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/diagrams/architecture-dark.png">
  <img src="docs/diagrams/architecture.png" alt="Architecture: the phone talks HTTPS to nginx (web), which serves the app and proxies /api to the Node api; the api stores JSON in ./data. The exercise media ship inside the web image; the AI coach and MCP server are optional." width="520">
</picture>
</p>

- **`frontend/`** is React 19 and Vite (React Router, Zustand), built to static files inside Docker.
- **`api/`** is plain `node:http` with three dependencies: `@simplewebauthn/server` for passkeys,
  `web-push` for notifications and `undici` for the AI coach's provider calls. Everything is
  stored as JSON under `./data`.
- **`web/`** builds the frontend and serves it with nginx, proxying `/api` so the whole app sits on
  one origin, which passkeys require.

The [architecture overview](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) has the longer version, with diagrams of the
frontend, sync, the exercise media and the watch.

The training logic (progression rules, 1RM, how a logged session is read back) lives in pure
functions under `frontend/src/lib/` with tests beside them. The HTTP API is documented as an
OpenAPI spec in [`api/openapi.yaml`](api/openapi.yaml), browsable at
[opengym.ch/api.html](https://opengym.ch/api.html).

### How sync works

Each profile's data is one document with a server revision. A device sends the revision it last
saw along with its changes; if another device wrote in between, the server refuses and returns the
current document so the device can merge and retry. Every change carries its own stamp, down to a
single setting or routine field, so the merge keeps the newest edit of each one and a deletion stays
deleted.

## Features

- **Browser Requests:** Make [XMLHttpRequests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest) directly from the browser.
- **Node.js Requests:** Make [http](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html) requests from Node.js environments.
- **Promise-based:** Fully supports the [Promise](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise) API for easier asynchronous code.
- **Interceptors:** Intercept requests and responses to add custom logic or transform data.
- **Data Transformation:** Transform request and response data automatically.
- **Request Cancellation:** Cancel requests using built-in mechanisms.
- **Automatic JSON Handling:** Automatically serializes and parses [JSON](https://www.json.org/json-en.html) data.
- **Form Serialization:** 🆕 Automatically serializes data objects to `multipart/form-data` or `x-www-form-urlencoded` formats.

## Installing

### Package manager

Using npm:

```bash
$ npm install axios
```

Using bower:

```bash

```

Using yarn:

```bash
$ yarn add axios
```

Using pnpm:

```bash
$ pnpm add axios
```

Using bun:

```bash
$ bun add axios
```

Once the package is installed, you can import the library using `import` or `require` approach:

```js
import axios, { isCancel, AxiosError } from "axios";
```

You can also use the default export, since the named export is just a re-export from the Axios factory:

```js
import axios from "axios";

console.log(axios.isCancel("something"));
```

If you use `require` for importing, **only the default export is available**:

```js
const axios = require("axios");

console.log(axios.isCancel("something"));
```

For some bundlers and some ES6 linters you may need to do the following:

```js
import { default as axios } from "axios";
```

you can try importing the module package directly:

```js
const axios = require("axios/dist/browser/axios.cjs"); // browser commonJS bundle (ES2017)
```

```js
import axios from "axios";
//const axios = require('axios'); // legacy way

try {
  const response = await axios.get("/user?ID=12345");
  console.log(response);
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error);
}

// Optionally the request above could also be done as
axios
  .get("/user", {
    params: {
      ID: 12345,
    },
  })
  .then(function (response) {
    console.log(response);
  })
  .catch(function (error) {
    console.log(error);
  })
  .finally(function () {
    // always executed
  });

// Want to use async/await? Add the `async` keyword to your outer function/method.
async function getUser() {
```

## Install

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

Optional: **ffmpeg** on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in `photos.mjs`. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.

## How 2.5 works

Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies `assets/` into the project, starts from `assets/starter.html` and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business (`software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service` or `place`) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup:

1. **Deal tokens and layout.** `scripts/start.mjs` deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind (`library/palettes.json`, `library/type.json`), and `assets/layout/deal.mjs` deals a hero layout (`split`, `centred`, `product`, `photo`, `place`, `collage`, `editorial`, `word`, `film`, `statement` or `triptych`).
2. **Start from one system.** `assets/starter.html`, `assets/system.css` and `assets/layout/layout.css` enforce one section per screen at desktop (`1440x900`), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer (`footer.closing`).
3. **Show real product UI and real photographs.** Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards (`assets/ui/cards.css`) with rewritten HTML UI fragments (`assets/ui/`) and node-and-line diagrams (`assets/diagrams/`), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by `scripts/icons.mjs`. Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs (`scripts/photos.mjs`, `assets/photos/`), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images.
4. **Keep effects for tech and gaming pages.** Shader grounds (`scripts/effects.mjs`), scroll scenes (`assets/scenes/`) and procedural 3D prints (`assets/objects/`) are dealt only on `software`, `tech` and `gaming` pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion. Every page gets a hero entrance and one or two moments from `scripts/moments.mjs`; cafes, hotels, shops, studios and services get only the photo- and type-led ones, and zero WebGL.
5. **Check in a real browser over HTTP.** `scripts/consistency.mjs`, `assets/layout/check.mjs`, `scripts/perf.mjs` and `scripts/shoot.mjs` render the built page in headless Chrome across `1440`, `1024`, `768` and `390`, catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. `scripts/gate.mjs` then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most.

Details of what changed from `2.1.x` are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

## The tools

Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/start.mjs` | Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the `<head>` links and `:root` tokens. |
| `assets/layout/deal.mjs` | Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; `assets/layout/check.mjs` checks it with long-headline stress tests. |
| `scripts/photos.mjs` | Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line. |
| `scripts/icons.mjs` | Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files. |
| `scripts/effects.mjs`, `scripts/moments.mjs` | Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind. |
| `scripts/gate.mjs`, `scripts/copy-lint.mjs` | The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs. |
| `scripts/consistency.mjs` | The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at `1440`, `1024`, `820`, `768` and `390` and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule. |
| `scripts/perf.mjs`, `scripts/shoot.mjs` | Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots. |

First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): `node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software` (kinds: `software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service`, `place`). Check a built page with `node scripts/consistency.mjs <url or file> --page <kind>`.

## Common Questions

**What does the skill need?**  
Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional (WebP photographs and the phone crop of a hero photograph). It installs nothing and uses no API keys. Bundled Commons photographs are stored locally; network access is used only when downloading additional photographs, Google Fonts or brand icons.

**Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?**  
From the skill's vetted photograph library (`assets/photos/photos.json`, including bundled Wikimedia Commons WebP sets and Unsplash photographs) dealt by `scripts/photos.mjs`. Library frames are used for trade and material details (or marked explicitly as draft stand-ins when the client has no photographs yet), never passed off as the client's own room, staff or product, and credited in one expandable footer line (`photos.mjs credits`).

**Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?**  
An empty folder gets a static page from `assets/starter.html`. An existing React, Vue, Svelte, Astro or Tailwind project is built in its own stack, with the kit served from its public folder; a Next.js brief is built as a static export. The browser checks run on the served or built page.

**When does a page get shaders or scroll effects?**  
Shaders only on `software`, `tech` (technical hardware) and `gaming` pages, and always within a four-context WebGL budget with static phone and reduced-motion fallbacks. Places, shops, cafes, hotels, studios, services and everyday physical products stay calm: photographs, sharp typography and flat colour, with a hero entrance and one or two photo- or type-led moments in their own sections.

标签描述图的视觉功能，不是论文领域。

| `pipeline` | 端到端阶段式数据流 | LRM, VidMan, LiveStar |
| `architecture` | 模型内部层与张量连接 | BLIP-2, Caduceus, Medusa |
| `taxonomy` | 任务、能力或数据全景 | EmbodiedBench, SimWorld |
| `teaser` | 经过版式设计的图文混排主视觉 | VIMA, PixArt-α |

# Spanish Top Tech Companies: MCP de empleo y salarios tech en España

<div align="center"><img alt="CI" src="https://github.com/pugarte7/spanish-top-tech-companies/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg"><img alt="Versión" src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/pugarte7/spanish-top-tech-companies?label=versi%C3%B3n"><img alt="MCP" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-spanishtoptechcompanies.com%2Fmcp-2b5cff"><img alt="Licencia del código: MIT" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/c%C3%B3digo-MIT-blue"><img alt="Licencia de los datos: CC BY-SA 4.0" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/datos-CC%20BY--SA%204.0-lightgrey"><img alt="Lenguaje" src="https://img.shields.io/github/languages/top/pugarte7/spanish-top-tech-companies"></div>

<p align="center">
🇪🇸 <a href="./README.md">Español</a> | 🇬🇧 <a href="./README.en.md">English</a>
</p>

Un servidor MCP que da a tu agente de IA los salarios reales de las empresas tech en España y sus ofertas abiertas, y aplica por ti. Cada día rastrea más de 400 portales de empleo: una media de más de 1.000 ofertas diarias a las que puedes aplicar directamente con el MCP. Detrás, una web con el ranking: **[spanishtoptechcompanies.com](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/es/)**.

## Contenido

- [Conecta tu agente](#conecta-tu-agente)
- [Cómo busca las ofertas](#cómo-busca-las-ofertas)
- [Aplica con tu agente](#aplica-con-tu-agente)
- [Herramientas del MCP](#herramientas-del-mcp)
- [La web](#la-web)
- [Cómo se calcula](#cómo-se-calcula)
- [Añade tu salario](#añade-tu-salario)
- [Contribuir](#contribuir)
- [Licencia](#licencia)
- [Aviso](#aviso)

## Conecta tu agente

Basta con este enlace. Añádelo como servidor MCP en tu agente, o pégaselo en el chat y que se conecte él:

```text
https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/mcp
```

Sin registro, sin claves y sin instalar nada. Funciona con cualquier agente que admita MCP: quienes lo usan lo hacen sobre todo con Codex y Cursor, y también sirven Claude, Claude Code, Instinct o Hermes.

En Hermes puedes instalar además la skill, que le enseña a usar el MCP y a aplicar por ti:

```text
hermes skills install pugarte7/spanish-top-tech-companies/skills/tech-pay-spain
```

Es gratis y lo mantiene una sola persona. Si te sirve, deja una estrella ⭐ arriba a la derecha: es lo que hace que lo encuentre más gente que busca trabajo en España.

## Cómo busca las ofertas

Más de 400 portales de empleo, más de 1.000 ofertas al día, todas con el sueldo de la empresa al lado.

- **Rastreo diario.** Cada mañana se leen los portales de empleo públicos de las empresas de la lista: Greenhouse, Workday, Ashby, Lever, SuccessFactors, Workable, Teamtailor, SmartRecruiters, Oracle y más.
- **Solo lo que puedes hacer desde España.** Se quedan las ofertas en España y las de remoto abiertas a España o a Europa.
- **Cada oferta, leída.** Del título salen el rol y el nivel, de la descripción los años de experiencia que pide y de la ubicación la comunidad autónoma.
- **Con el sueldo al lado.** Cada oferta lleva el sueldo base mediano de la empresa para ese rol en España, y de cuánta gente sale.
- **Filtros que entienden lo que pides.** Texto con sinónimos (SRE es site reliability), rol o especialidad (backend, frontend, DevOps), región o remoto, modalidad, nivel, tus años de experiencia, empresa y sueldo mínimo. El sueldo mínimo se compara con el que publica la oferta, si lo publica, y si no con la mediana de la empresa.
- **Nunca te deja con las manos vacías.** Si nada encaja, dice cuántas ofertas quita cada filtro y propone las más cercanas.
- **Sin repetir.** Las ofertas que ya has visto o a las que ya has aplicado no vuelven a salir.
- **Aplicas desde el mismo MCP.** `job_questions` lee en directo el formulario de la oferta (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, Recruitee, Teamtailor, BambooHR, Pinpoint, Rippling, Eightfold y Workday con tu cuenta) y marca qué preguntas respondes tú y cuáles el agente.

## Aplica con tu agente

Tu agente busca entre esas ofertas, lee el formulario, escribe la carta y las respuestas a partir de tu CV, te enseña la solicitud completa y la envía cuando le dices que sí.

<img alt="Tu agente, conectado al MCP, busca ofertas de backend en remoto de empresas que pagan más de 80.000 €, encuentra 16 en cinco empresas, rellena el formulario de Pleo con tu CV, te pregunta las tres respuestas que le faltan y envía la solicitud cuando le dices que sí" src="docs/img/mcp-demo.es.gif" width="100%">

1. **Dale tu CV y lo que buscas.** Una sola vez, en el chat: tu CV, dónde y cómo quieres trabajar, el sueldo que pides y tu permiso de trabajo.
2. **Dile que aplique.** Por ejemplo:

   > Aplica por mí a las ofertas de las empresas de spanishtoptechcompanies.com que pagan 60.000 € o más a alguien con mi experiencia en Madrid.

   O: «Aplica a 5 ofertas de backend en Barcelona», «Aplica a las ofertas en remoto que pueda hacer desde España».
3. **Revisa y da el sí.** Ves cada solicitud completa antes de que salga.

<img alt="Más de 400 portales y más de 1.000 ofertas al día llegan a find_jobs; con tu CV, find_jobs encuentra ofertas con el sueldo de la empresa, job_questions lee el formulario, el agente escribe la carta y las respuestas y, si das el sí, la envía con su navegador y lo anota con report_application" src="docs/img/apply-flow.es.svg" width="100%">

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Nada se envía sin tu sí. Las preguntas delicadas, como sueldo o permiso de trabajo, te las hace una vez, todas en un mensaje, y los consentimientos de privacidad los aceptas tú.

> [!NOTE]
> La web no guarda nada tuyo. Tu perfil y tus solicitudes se quedan en tu agente, en su memoria o en un archivo como `~/job-search.md`. Si al ir a enviarla no tiene navegador, instala uno (primero un Chromium integrado, luego Claude in Chrome, luego el servidor MCP de Playwright) y lo usa en segundo plano, sin ventana, para no molestarte; solo si no puede, te da el enlace y las respuestas para que la envíes tú. Si un formulario pide un CAPTCHA, te pasa la página. Si una empresa manda un código por correo, lo lee de tu correo si se lo conectas, o te lo pide.

## Herramientas del MCP

El servidor se llama `tech-pay-spain`. Tu agente elige la herramienta; no tienes que nombrarla.

| Herramienta | Qué hace | Parámetros |
|---|---|---|
| `find_jobs` | Busca entre las más de 1.000 ofertas abiertas del día por rol, stack, sector o idioma, cada una con el sueldo base mediano de la empresa para ese rol. Si nada encaja, dice qué filtro sobra y propone las más cercanas. | `query`, `role`, `region`, `workplace`, `seniority`, `years`, `company`, `min_salary_eur`, `exclude`, `limit` |
| `job_questions` | Lee en directo el formulario de una oferta: cada pregunta, si es obligatoria y si la respondes tú o el agente, y el enlace para aplicar. | `id` |
| `application_guide` | El procedimiento para aplicar por alguien y la plantilla de notas que guarda el agente. | `client` |
| `report_application` | Cómo fue cada solicitud: enviada, incierta (se envió y nada lo confirmó), fallida y por qué, o en tus manos, y qué hizo falta para enviarla. No lleva nada sobre ti. | `id`, `status`, `reason`, `browser`, `steps`, `attempts`, `notes` |
| `salary_stats` | Sueldo base mediano, horquilla (p25-p75), total mediano y cuánta gente cobra 60.000 € o más. | `role`, `region`, `years` |
| `top_companies` | Las empresas que más pagan para un rol, región y experiencia. | `role`, `region`, `years`, `search`, `limit` |
| `company_salaries` | Lo que paga una empresa, en total y por rol, región o experiencia. | `name`, `role`, `region`, `years` |
| `list_filters` | Roles, regiones, tramos de experiencia y fecha de los datos. | |

<details>
<summary>Para desarrolladores</summary>

- Streamable HTTP en `https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/mcp`, sin autenticación y con CORS abierto.
- El mismo servidor por stdio, con Node 22 o posterior y sin dependencias: `node scripts/mcp-stdio.mjs`.
- Los datos en [data.json](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/api/v1/data.json), las ofertas en [jobs.json](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/api/v1/jobs.json) y un resumen en [llms.txt](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/llms.txt).
- Una [skill para agentes](skills/tech-pay-spain/SKILL.md) con cómo leer las cifras.

</details>

## La web

[spanishtoptechcompanies.com](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/es/) muestra lo mismo que el MCP, para mirarlo tú:

- **Ranking de empresas tech** en España por sueldo base mediano, con buscador.
- **Salarios por rol**: ingeniería de software, producto, datos, diseño, gestión y más de 30 roles.
- **Salarios por comunidad autónoma** en un mapa.
- **Sueldo según la experiencia**, de 0 a más de 20 años.
- **Remoto, híbrido o presencial**.
- **Base y total**, con bonus y acciones.

Los salarios se actualizan cada semana y las ofertas cada día.

## Cómo se calcula

Cada salario viene de [Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi) y solo cuenta si la ubicación de esa persona está en España. Aparecen todas las empresas, paguen lo que paguen, ordenadas por la mediana de su sueldo base; cada una tiene página de LinkedIn o web, y tiene en Levels.fyi al menos 5 salarios de cualquier país sumando todos los roles: una empresa que nadie más ha reportado no aparece. Las empresas con menos de 3 salarios se listan después de las demás. Los salarios se resumen por empresa, rol, región y experiencia, y los importes se redondean a 1.000 €. Los detalles están en [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md#the-website-and-the-mcp-server).

## Añade tu salario

Súbelo a [Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi/salaries/add). La lista se rehace con los salarios de España que hay allí, así que cuenta desde la siguiente actualización. Es anónimo. Si sabes de primera mano lo que paga una empresa, o tienes una oferta por escrito, abre un [issue](../../issues/new?template=update-band.yml).

## Contribuir

Los pull requests son bienvenidos: el pipeline, la metodología, la web, el MCP o las comprobaciones. [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md) explica las reglas y [docs/CONTEXT.md](docs/CONTEXT.md) lo que ha salido mal antes y por qué el código es como es. Si quieres hablarlo antes, abre un [issue](../../issues/new/choose).

## Licencia

El código es [MIT](LICENSE) y los datos de `data/` [CC BY-SA 4.0](LICENSE-DATA). Los salarios se leen de [Levels.fyi](https://www.levels.fyi) y siguen sujetos a sus condiciones.

> Data source: Levels.fyi (https://www.levels.fyi)

## Aviso

Proyecto independiente, sin relación con Levels.fyi ni con ninguna de las empresas. Las cifras resumen salarios que otras personas han reportado. Pueden estar incompletas, desactualizadas o mal, y no son ofertas ni asesoramiento financiero o legal. Si quieres que se quite o corrija algo, sobre una empresa o sobre ti, abre un [issue](../../issues/new/choose) o escribe a ugartep117@gmail.com. Quién está detrás y qué datos se tratan: [aviso legal y privacidad](https://spanishtoptechcompanies.com/es/legal/).

2. **AI 原生证据链** — 单函数 dossier（伪代码 + CFG + 调用关系 + 栈帧，同一数据库修订）、持久调查任务、stale 证据标记、共享调用预算——把"模型推测"与"已验证结论"分开，这是给 AI 用的逆向工作台与 GUI 套壳的本质区别。
3. **零配置自包含** — 完整安装包内置 Ghidra/JDK/Python 与 x64dbg/bridge 及上游源码、许可与哈希清单，一次解压 + 一条 PowerShell 命令完成安装，全程不需要商业 IDA。
4. **审批安全模型** — 13 个修改/执行入口全部经过宿主审批（`allowed-once`），配合 Undo、审计流水与 SHA-256 哈希清单，适合团队与教学环境的可控授权分析。
5. **增长最快的 DSH 逆向插件** — 上线 90 天 4,100+ Stars、530+ Forks，Star 增速居 DSH 插件生态首位；85 篇文档与 Release 节奏持续更新。

## ❓ FAQ（高频问题直答）

**IG5 是什么？**
无限五代（Infinite Gen 5 / IG5，仓库 `dsh-infinite-gen-5`）是面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的开源逆向工程插件与可视化工作台，提供 43 个工具、8 个工作流技能，把 Ghidra 静态分析、x64dbg 原生调试、Unicorn 仿真、HTTP/HTTPS 流量采集与解密、多智能体调查协作整合进同一套 DSH 工作流。

**IG5 与 IDA Pro / Binary Ninja 是什么关系？**
互补而非替代。IG5 使用 Ghidra 作为静态后端并内置完整运行时，**安装 IG5 不需要购买任何商业反编译器授权**；已有 IDA 的用户也可以通过 `ig5_run_idapython`（审批入口）在授权环境中复用现有脚本。

**IG5 免费吗？采用什么许可证？**
免费开源，采用 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0（署名-非商业性使用-相同方式共享）。可自由用于个人研究、安全审计、CTF 与教学；商业售卖、付费倒卖与二开商用被明确禁止，详见文末许可声明。

**怎么安装 IG5？**
Windows x64 用户从 [v1.3.0 Release](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases/tag/v1.3.0) 下载自包含安装包，解压后在根目录执行 `& .\plugin\install.ps1`，重启 DSH 后用 `/ig5 engines` 验证。完整步骤见[快速安装](#local-install)。

**IG5 支持哪些平台？**
Windows x64 完整支持（安装包内置全部运行时）；macOS Apple Silicon 提供实验性 Ghidra 静态车道；目标侧支持 x86/x64/ARM64 等架构的静态分析。详见 [macOS 指南](docs/MACOS_RUNTIME.md) 与 [DSH 兼容记录](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md)。

**IG5 能做什么、不能做什么？**
能做：静态分析、可视化 CFG 工作台、原生调试、单函数仿真、流量采集与 TLS 解密、XOR/AES 解密候选、协议分帧与状态建模、CFF/VM 去混淆研究、子代理协作调查。边界：所有执行/修改类操作需宿主审批；不承诺"任意保护一键脱壳"；局部模型不外推为通用恢复。完整口径见 [能力矩阵](docs/CAPABILITIES.md) 与 [已知限制](docs/LIMITATIONS.md)。

**IG5 和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？**
完全独立的第三方开源项目，与 DeepSeek 官方或其关联主体无隶属、无商业合作、无官方背书。IG5 通过 DSH 插件机制扩展宿主能力，DSH 本身不随 IG5 分发。

**为什么 IG5 要做 13 个审批门？**
安全模型设计。所有修改字节、执行样本、仿真、重放、采集控制入口都必须经宿主显式审批（`allowed-once`），配合 Undo、审计流水与 SHA-256 哈希清单，让 AI 驱动的逆向操作在授权范围内可审计、可控、可回溯——这是 IG5 与"裸工具包"类插件的核心差异。

**IG5 的版本节奏如何？**
2026-08-15 创建以来已发布 v1.0.0、v1.1.0、v1.3.0 三个正式版本（90 天内），当前最新版 v1.3.0（2026-10-27）将工具面扩展至 Full 43 并新增 APK/固件静态前端、API trace 与 CFF 状态分析。历史版本见 [Releases](https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5/releases)。

**如何在论文/报告中引用 IG5？**
推荐引用格式：`Minglink, "Infinite Gen 5 (IG5): An Open-Source Reverse-Engineering Workbench Plugin for DeepSeek Harness", GitHub repository dsh-infinite-gen-5, 2026. https://github.com/Minglink/dsh-infinite-gen-5`（引用时请注明所用版本号与访问日期）。

## Install a Plugin

For most users, the **Awesome Copilot** marketplace is already registered in the Copilot CLI/VS Code, so you can install a plugin directly:

```bash
copilot plugin install <plugin-name>@awesome-copilot
```

If you are using an older Copilot CLI version or a custom setup and see an error that the marketplace is unknown, register it once and then install:

```bash
copilot plugin marketplace add github/awesome-copilot
copilot plugin install <plugin-name>@awesome-copilot
```
